name: ClubAL
summary: ClubAL organizes institutional routines on Windows, publishes what displays need and provides read-only access.
promise: A local flow for recording, publishing and reading without mixing responsibilities.

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Operational information gets lost when every environment improvises.
tabs.body: Spreadsheets, paper and scattered messages create different versions of the same routine. ClubAL centralizes records on the responsible PC and separates editing from reading.

tabs.label: Three modules
tabs.title: Each module handles one part of the work.
tabs.body: The product separates responsibilities across three modules: Operação records and publishes; Rotinas displays only approved information; Consulta provides authorized reading without opening editing.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The product can be demonstrated and deployment remains assisted.
tabs.body: Automated checks cover Windows flows, offline mode and publishing rules. Installations, displays and physical networks remain subject to review in their real environment.
points: Windows packages are not code-signed yet

tabs.label: Game
tabs.title: An adult protagonist in a world that records consequences.
tabs.body: Dun Caerwyn, House Roscaern and its systems make body, blood and memory shape Maeve’s journey, narrative and combat.

tabs.label: Production
tabs.title: The scale is designed for one person to finish.
tabs.body: Compact areas, modular kits and concentrated detail preserve the mood without promising a world larger than solo production can support.

tabs.label: The Architect
tabs.title: The Architect connects authorship and consequence.
tabs.body: My image as The Architect is a conceptual easter egg about authorship and consequence. It inspires the project without claiming that the character is already playable.
points: Concept is not presented as gameplay

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The first combat slice has a technical foundation.
tabs.body: Light combo, dodge and Blood First now form part of Phase 8. Technical gates passed; combat feel, rhythm and readability are still being evaluated.

name: Demonyza
kicker: Digital presence case for a content creator
summary: The website brings profile, schedule, streams and community together in a responsive experience for mobile and desktop.
promise: Content and community in an original digital presence that is recognizable and easy to navigate.
imageAlt: Current Demonyza homepage with purple visual identity, navigation and interactive areas

tabs.label: Challenge
tabs.title: More than a link page.
tabs.body: The starting point was to introduce the creator, organize her public channels and give the community clear routes without erasing the client’s identity.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: The client’s identity, with clear navigation.
tabs.body: Profile, schedule, Twitch, Discord and OpenDota form an original responsive experience for mobile and desktop.
points: Easy return to the main flow

tabs.label: Delivery
tabs.title: Live and maintained independently.
tabs.body: The website is live on Cloudflare Pages; the client’s code remains protected in a private repository.

name: Codex Checkpoint
kicker: A local queue for validations and decisions
summary: Codex Checkpoint preserves pending validations, decisions and feedback across work sessions.
promise: Pending work resumes at the right time with context and decisions intact.
imageAlt: Codex Checkpoint showing a fictional queue of pending validations, decisions and note history

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Not every test can be completed during the session.
tabs.body: Gameplay, visual review, devices, authentication and practical decisions may require another moment or environment. Without a queue, that context disappears.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: A checkpoint queue — not another chat.
tabs.body: Each checkpoint records enough context to return to the pending task and leave a decision or actionable feedback.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: A native, installable application.
tabs.body: Interface, command line and file integration form one product. Current builds are not code-signed yet, and that limit remains clearly stated.

name: NEXUS
kicker: A Windows hub for local projects
summary: NEXUS brings projects, paths and checks into one local hub that shows what is ready and what needs attention.
promise: The right path appears before execution — without hunting through shortcuts.
imageAlt: Current NEXUS overview with two fictional projects, readiness states, update dates and an option to add a project.

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Multiple projects outgrew a pile of shortcuts.
tabs.body: Each product has its own builds, tools and checks; the right path needs to appear before anything runs.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: A local command desk replaces the pile of shortcuts.
tabs.body: Projects and paths are added from the interface; NEXUS only adopts a newer alternative when the match is safe and unambiguous.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The local foundation is validated and in use.
tabs.body: Projects and checks open in development context, without a required login and without mixing product runtimes.

name: Local First Checklist
summary: An open-source Python application demonstrates a local JSON checklist, command line, tests and CI.
promise: Local-first architecture demonstrated in a compact, verifiable example.
imageAlt: Illustration of a local checklist with completed items and a JSON file

tabs.label: Scope
tabs.title: Small enough to understand end to end.
tabs.body: Tasks remain in a local JSON file, with simple operations available through the command line.

tabs.label: Quality
tabs.title: Simplicity still needs evidence.
tabs.body: Unit tests, Python compilation and a smoke test protect the main operations without adding infrastructure to the application.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: Version 1.0.0 is published.
tabs.body: The published version brings together structure, documentation, tests and a coherent architectural choice within a limited scope.

name: C7 Engineering System
kicker: A local engineering system for Codex
summary: C7 coordinates context, risk, execution and validation so Codex can move autonomously without losing human control.
promise: More autonomy where it is safe. More control where it matters.
imageAlt: C7 Engineering System organizing complex flows around a core with seven balanced facets
cardImageAlt: Project flows converging on the C7 monogram and seven coordinated facets

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: More capability cannot compensate for the wrong context.
tabs.body: Development assistants fail not only from limited capability, but from unclear scope, disproportionate depth or closure without proof. C7 establishes the contract before execution.

tabs.label: How it works
tabs.title: A compact core activates depth only when it adds value.
tabs.body: C7 reads project rules, classifies risk from R0 to R4 and invokes proportional skills, knowledge and review—a coherent answer, not a queue of voices.

tabs.label: Evidence
tabs.title: Architecture becomes a product only when it survives testing and return.
tabs.body: Version 1.0.0 passed 42 Pester tests, 24 checks in the installed environment, comparative evaluations and byte-for-byte restoration in a disposable profile.

tabs.label: Environment
tabs.title: Execution adapts to the available machine.
tabs.body: Before heavy work, C7 checks CPU, memory, paging and storage. In a constrained environment, it serializes stages, reduces pressure and reuses completed validation.

tabs.label: Control
tabs.title: Technical autonomy without outsourcing authority.
tabs.body: Routine decisions proceed autonomously within scope. Publication, credentials, costs and hard-to-reverse operations remain behind explicit human approval.

faq.title: From request to delivery, without losing context or control.
faq.intro: C7 turns a request into engineering work: it understands the environment, sizes the risk, executes at the right depth and closes with evidence.

items.question: What problem does C7 solve?
items.answer: It prevents development assistants from moving forward with the wrong context, excessive rigor for simple work or insufficient verification for critical changes. The system calibrates the work before execution.

items.question: What changes in practice?
items.answer: Every task gains an observable outcome, protected scope, proportional execution and completion evidence. Decisions and checkpoints remain available so valid work can resume without being repeated.

items.question: How does it adjust rigor for each task?
items.answer: C7 classifies risk from R0 to R4 using reach, reversibility, data, privilege, external effect and cost of error. Depth increases only when the impact justifies it.

items.question: Why does the system use seven lenses?
items.answer: Architecture, human experience, second-order effects, operations, alternatives, security and closure are checked together. They are not seven bots: the result remains one coherent decision.

items.question: How far does autonomy go?
items.answer: C7 handles routine technical decisions within the authorized scope. External, destructive, financial or hard-to-reverse actions remain behind objective human approval.

items.question: How does it adapt to different projects, teams and machines?
items.answer: Project rules continue to prevail, and computer capacity is checked on demand. C7 installs no daemon and does not force the same load or ceremony on every environment.

items.question: What has already been proven?
items.answer: Version 1.0.0 is active and healthy. The release passed 42 Pester tests, 24 installed checks, comparative evaluations and a byte-for-byte rollback in a disposable environment.

faq.closing: C7 already works as an independent layer and is not officially affiliated with OpenAI. Its architecture can be discussed for adoption, integration or product evolution.
